The island's sole entrance, featuring a plaza, flowers, sculptures, and giant balloons. It is the starting point of the entire island of dreams.
The liveliest spot on Starland, where everyone exchanges moves through dance battles, blending applause with footsteps. It has become the place on the island with the most cheers.
This Boarlet carousel breaks all expectations and has become a delightfully odd local legend—where everyone can't help but squeal at the adorable little Boarlets...
A massive DJ booth, playing a variety of music, stands on Silver Gull Beach. Decorated with seashells and sunlight, even the tides turn into a melodious tune here.

The blooming Cherry Blossom Forest has become one of the most beautiful spots on Starland. Visitors come here to picnic, enjoy the scenery, take photos, and admire the massive Star Orbiter in the distance.

The massive Star Orbiter seems close enough to touch the stars, lifting visitors to the clouds where hidden feelings can finally be spoken. It has become the perfect place on Starland to while away the hours.

On a table no larger than a few inches, you might see grand simulations that decide the fate of nations, or a simple contest settled with a single gold coin. The Starland Club is such a place—fair and just, filled with the cheers of victors and the sighs of the defeated. But what does it matter? It's just a game.

Starland's founder, Meowclu, said that the sea and sky get lonely at night too. If we don't hang a lantern high enough, those playful stars might not find their way home. And so, the "Starlight" was built—a watchtower overlooking the entire island.
One of Starland's famous landmarks. Its unique heart shape sometimes tempts tourists to toss coins in and make a wish when staff aren't looking.
Heart-Shaped Pond - Not a Wishing Pool
Thanks to Starland's seaside design, the beach and sea here are authentic, making it perfect for visitors seeking a quiet, slow-paced getaway.
One of Starland's main roads, often used as a meeting point. Its enduring popularity may come from being the best spot to watch the Ee-chan Drum Band.

The lights of the Aurora Stage are more than mere illumination—they carry messages.
This idea stems from the bold vision of the founder, Meowclu: if signals from distant other worlds could be captured, just like the aurora itself, then the boundaries of this isolated dream island might one day be broken.

One of the liveliest game zones on Starland. It hosts various Nappo-themed activities and is the best place to get up close with Nappos. As for whether the Nappos here might suddenly pull out weapons and attack visitors... well, that likely depends on whether the Meowlux Merchant Guild pays them on time.

The original blueprint for the sightseeing train was grand enough to fit half the Merchant Guild, but it was vetoed by Miss Meowclu with the remark, "Carriages would only slow it down." Thus, the Beep-Beep Express retained only its locomotive. Though a little cramped, it lends the journey a touch of unexpected warmth.

A corner of West Beach that seems quiet but is actually the densest spot for ghost stories on Starland, thanks to its proximity to the House of Wonders.
If you want to stumble upon someone walking an Arachnocrab or an eccentric detective testing dreams with a tiny vial... come here to discover rumors and ghost stories all your own.
After the Asterleeds Independence War, Hero's Herb grew in Ancient City of Vill, spreading towards Asterleeds.
It is said to be a divine ruins left by the Bapharia civilization, standing in the center of Asteria Plains.

The Asterleeds Independence War was seen as unjust by the Bapharian Creed. Many tree carvings were spontaneously built by the people to quietly commemorate the heroes who brought independence and peace.
A resting post built after the war, adjacent to the old battlefield of Andra Basin. Some "battlefield scavengers" live here, searching for gear left over from the Asterleeds Independence War.
An untamed and hazardous expanse, once a major battlefield in the Asterleeds Independence War, where wild-growing natural plants coexist harmoniously with war remnants.

Deep within the Andra Basin tunnels, where the Byrnhald's Giant Golem was destroyed during the Asterleeds Independence War-its abandoned energy core continues to trigger dramatic ecological transformations.
Minsterhorn was once a peaceful small village, destroyed by the flames of war during the Asterleeds Independence War. The surviving villagers returned here after the war to rebuild their homes.
The Kanamia Tribe lives by hunting and gathering, maintaining a non-contact, unwelcoming attitude towards outsiders, with defensive checkpoints set up around the tribe.
The place where the chieftain and elders of the Kanamia Tribe hold meetings and discuss matters.
A mysterious ruin, one of the sacred sites of the Bapharian Creed. Seems that humans once lived here long ago...
The Dark Mist Legion, which aims to defeat Asterleeds, has established a secret base within the Ruins of Andra City.
The Fallen River takes its name from the deep valley it flows through. At the bottom of the valley lies a shallow inlet that displays spectacular scenes.

The northern highlands are rich in waterways, dotted with countless waterfalls. Fed by melting snow from the mountains, they eventually gather into the Fallen River, nourishing the intricate ecosystem.
Xeno Engram has reshaped the highland's ecology, causing strange stone spires to erupt from the ground. The sharp rocks pierce upward, pointing straight toward the Pillar of Divinity.
The smoke from hearths and the voices of the past have long faded. All that remains of those settlements are silent hollows in the rock walls.
Hidden within the river's cliff walls is a path leading to an abandoned ruin. Now occupied by monsters, it has become a place where darkness festers.
The Bahamar Highlands are covered with dazzling crystalline flora known as Illusory Blooms. They are beautiful yet dangerous.
According to scholars, these sharp rocks sprouting from crevices display clear growth layers and still continue to grow at an extremely slow rate.
Though the highlands are scarce in resources, Pilgrims constantly come here to worship the Pillar of Divinity. They cultivated crops on this land, and over time, a village took shape.
As the largest ruin on the Continent of Magna, the Pillar of Divinity is sealed and guarded by the Creed. Though entry is forbidden, countless Pilgrims still come in reverence.
Influenced by Xeno Engram, the highlands are unnaturally rich in mineral resources. The Duchy of Byrnhald established Sislesa Mine here and stationed troops to oversee extraction.
Years of excavation have nearly depleted all surface mineral deposits. To maintain output, the Blackstone Legion constructed an underground mining zone.
Ore from the Sislesa Mine is sent through the mining tunnels to the Bekmar Transport Station for initial sorting, then transported by armored vehicles back to the Duchy of Byrnhald.
As the mine's overseers, the Blackstone Legion stations itself on the nearby hill. The domineering Garrison Outpost looms over the entire mining district like a tower.
With miners flooding in, a complete ecosystem gradually formed around the mining area, including stores, eateries, and watchtowers.
Raw ore must undergo initial sorting at the Transport Station, and the Squad has built massive, costly sorting machines for that.
Steel Beast of the Transport Station
The Blackstone Legion stores supplies and trains soldiers here. Terrifying sounds of drills and battle cries often echo from within, and no locals would get near it.
Built against the cliff, the Mustard Tavern is the soldiers' only place of leisure. Its two levels are strictly divided, and the upper level serves only Blackstone soldiers and officers.
The lower level of Mustard Tavern is dim and sunless, with no seating provided. Miners stack crates into makeshift stools just to have a brief rest.
The Transport Station once handled both land and water transport. But as surface mining drained the area's minerals, water levels dropped, and the docks fell into abandonment.
A Corner of the Transport Station
A giant Illusory Bloom near the Pillar of Divinity spreads its vast root system, concealing an entrance beneath it.
Illusory Bloom Under the Pillar of Divinity
As the Blackstone Legion's relentless mining extended deeper underground, countless mineshafts were carved out. But once a mineshaft was exhausted, it would be abandoned and forgotten.
An abandoned mineshaft is like a forgotten scar. Though left unmanaged, the passageways slowly heal over the years, giving rise to new greenery.
The Illusory Blooms are drawn to stone. Wherever minerals and crystals are abundant, Illusory Blooms flourish.
Illusory Bloom in the Underground Mine
Illusory Blooms grow thick throughout the underground tunnels, giving rise to endless rumors and ghost stories. Some claim to have seen Nappo wandering among them in a moment of daze.
Ore extracted from the underground is temporarily stored in the transfer zone before being transported to the surface.
The Rock Serpents in the underground mines are ferocious, leaving even the Blackstone Legion helpless. All they can do is build heavy Isolation Gates to hold them back.
The tangled depths of the excavation area are where miners are most likely to go missing.
At the very bottom of the underground mines lies a repository for mysterious crystals...
Even in these dark tunnels, there are places where faint sunlight manages to seep in.
These dark stone pillars are covered in rough patterns and shrouded in a murky gray, probably once violently damaged.

Although humans haven't yet figured out how to activate Golems, some experts have managed to build a few replicas based on the Legacy... reportedly reaching 66% of the original's power. Please assist with testing them and repel the monsters in the rift.
To evaluate the melee performance of the replica Golems, civilian Legacy experts have initiated a combat test. Repel the formidable enemies in the rift to complete the final assessment.
The courier has encountered unexpected obstacles in the highlands. Adventurers are needed to escort the supplies and ensure the route stays clear.
The rugged mountain route has become treacherous once again. Adventurers are needed to help the courier navigate the hazards and deliver the supplies safely.
When conflict arises among monsters, they call upon the strong to intervene. Choose a side and help suppress the opposition to end the conflict.
The conflict has flared up again! This time, both sides want your help. Pick a faction and join the battle to bring the conflict to a decisive end.
